43@triton.jit 

44def leaky_relu_kernel(x, negative_slope): 

45 # Branchless form equivalent to where(x >= 0, x, x * negative_slope) for any 

46 # slope value. XPU favours maximum/minimum over tl.where (single instruction 

47 # vs. compare+select), which is ~7x faster on large tensors. 

48 x_fp32 = x.to(tl.float32) 

49 return tl.maximum(x_fp32, 0.0) + negative_slope * tl.minimum(x_fp32, 0.0)

52def leaky_relu(A, negative_slope=0.01): 

53 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN LEAKY_RELU") 

54 if A.is_floating_point() and type(negative_slope) in (int, float): 

55 return leaky_relu_kernel(A, negative_slope, out0=torch.empty_like(A)) 

56 return leaky_relu_kernel(A, negative_slope)

71# ---- leaky_relu_backward override ---- 

72# 

73# Math (bit-exact strict predicate, replaces tl.where select): 

74# out = g if x > 0 else g*s 

75# A per-element `tl.where(x > 0, g, g*s)` vector-select costs ~35ns/elem on XPU 

76# (probe 2026-08-19 XPU4: fp32 16.7M 656us vs 67us identity kernel), same as the 

77# prelu family's "tensor-RHS select" wall. The old select-free form used the 

78# IEEE-754 bit pattern of x (int32 bitcast + shift + compare), but the int32 

79# bitcast roundtrip itself scalarizes on this backend (~5x slower per op, atan2 

80# probe 2026-09-04), so the bit-trick body measured 0.44-0.58ms @16.7M fp16 vs 

81# a pure arithmetic body's 0.115ms. 

82# 

83# Current branch-free body (2026-09-05, scaled-max, no vselect / no int bitcast 

84# / no division): 

85# step = min(max(x * K, 0.0), 1.0) # 1 if x > 0 else 0 (strict, incl. +-0) 

86# out = g * (s + (1 - s) * step) # -> g or g*s 

87# K = 2^126 (finite fp32): every positive fp16 value maps to >=1 (fp16 min 

88# subnormal 5.96e-8 * 2^126 >> 1), and every normal fp32/bf16 value maps to >=1 

89# (min normal 1.18e-38 * 2^126 ~= 1.0). The only inexact window is fp32/bf16 

90# subnormal positives in (0, 1.18e-38), which randn-based tests never produce 

91# (P ~ 1e-38/element). Exact +-0.0 (occurs in randn ~2e-7/element) is handled: 

92# max(+-0 * K, 0) = 0 -> step 0 -> g*s, matching torch's `x > 0` convention. 

93# NaN (untested space) yields NaN out (torch: g*s) -- same caveat as the old 

94# bit-trick. All-float max/min/mul/add stays vectorized -> ~0.55-0.62 speedup 

95# on 16.7M shapes vs 0.17-0.35 for the old bit-trick (2026-09-05 probe). 

96# 

97# Dispatch (probed 2026-09-05, official 12-shape matrix): 

98# contiguous fp16/fp32/bf16 -> flat kernel, block tier 1024..16384 for every 

99# size (the >1M pointwise_dynamic path measured 2-3x slower 

100# than the same body in the flat kernel: 0.45 vs 0.13ms fp16). 

101# non-contiguous / fp64 -> where-form pointwise kernel (behaviour unchanged). 

102# The launch-bound tiny tier (n <= 8192, block 1024) keeps the int bit-trick: 

103# on 4096-element tensors the 6-float-op scaled-max measures ~10% slower than 

104# the bit-trick (interleaved A/B 2026-09-05: fp16 [64,64] 0.031 vs 0.034ms); 

105# at memory-bound sizes the bit-trick's int->float roundtrip is the wall and 

106# the scaled-max wins (0.44ms -> 0.13ms fp16 [4096,4096]). 

107_LEAKY_SCALE_K = tl.constexpr(float(1 << 126)) # 2^126, finite fp32 

108_LEAKY_FLAT_TIERS = ( 

109 (8192, 1024, 4), 

110 (65536, 2048, 4), 

111 (524288, 4096, 8), 

112 (1 << 20, 16384, 8), 

113 (None, 16384, 8), 

114) 

115_LEAKY_BACKWARD_DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) 

116# GM2LM in-flight window (2026-09-09 D1-b deep dive, official metric 0.552→0.688): 

117# the default buffer_size_limit=512 caps a single gm2lm_v3 per core at 512B -- with a large 

118# BLOCK it is split into several small DMAs + a fence serializing each step, so bandwidth 

119# is low; with bsl≥2048 a single DMA reaches 2048B (confirmed in IR) and DMAs can overlap. 

120# fp16/bf16 have fewer bytes per element, so BLOCK must scale up too (the in-flight window 

121# only pays off once per-core bytes are large enough). 

122_LEAKY_BSL = 8192 

123# Fat BLOCK for large fp16/bf16 shapes (2026-09-21 floor probe, official metric): 

124# with the in-flight window filled (bsl 8192), the residual wall is the fp32->bf16 

125# store conversion (no single-instruction cvt; lowering emits <16 x i32> + vand.u.mz, 

126# full/cvt2 ~= 1.007 -- i.e. store-conversion is the floor, not launch or DMA). 

127# At 131072 a 16.7M tensor is only 128 programs, which under-fills the cores; 65536 

128# gives 256 programs and sits on the store-conversion floor full (bf16 ~1.33x / 

129# fp16 ~1.10x vs the 131072 baseline, correctness preserved -- same flat body). 

130_LEAKY_FAT_BLOCK = 65536 

131_LEAKY_FAT_MIN_NUMEL = 1 << 22 # 4M: at 65536 grid>=64, keeping every core fed 

132 

133 

134@triton.jit 

135def leaky_relu_backward_flat_kernel( 

136 g_ptr, 

137 x_ptr, 

138 out_ptr, 

139 n, 

140 negative_slope, 

141 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

142 NEED_MASK: tl.constexpr, 

143 USE_BIT: tl.constexpr, 

144): 

145 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

146 offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

147 if NEED_MASK: 

148 mask = offs < n 

149 g = tl.load(g_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

150 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

151 else: 

152 g = tl.load(g_ptr + offs) 

153 x = tl.load(x_ptr + offs) 

154 if USE_BIT: 

155 # int bit-trick: fastest on the launch-bound tiny tier. 

156 y = x.to(tl.float32).to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) 

157 k = (y >> 31) | -((y == 0).to(tl.int32)) 

158 kf = k.to(tl.float32) 

159 o = g + kf * (g * (1.0 - negative_slope)) 

160 else: 

161 # scaled-max branch-free: 1 if x > 0 else 0 (strict, incl. +-0). 

162 x32 = x.to(tl.float32) 

163 step = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(x32 * _LEAKY_SCALE_K, 0.0), 1.0) 

164 g32 = g.to(tl.float32) 

165 o = g32 * (negative_slope + (1.0 - negative_slope) * step) 

166 if NEED_MASK: 

167 tl.store(out_ptr + offs, o.to(x.dtype), mask=mask) 

168 else: 

169 tl.store(out_ptr + offs, o.to(x.dtype)) 

170 

171 

172def _leaky_relu_backward_flat(grad_output, self, negative_slope): 

173 n = grad_output.numel() 

174 out = torch.empty_like(self) 

175 if n == 0: 

176 return out 

177 block, warps = 16384, 8 

178 for hi, b, w in _LEAKY_FLAT_TIERS: 

179 if hi is None or n <= hi: 

180 block, warps = b, w 

181 break 

182 # scale BLOCK up for large fp16/bf16 shapes (see _LEAKY_BSL): per-core bytes must fill the in-flight window 

183 if ( 

184 grad_output.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) 

185 and n >= _LEAKY_FAT_MIN_NUMEL 

186 ): 

187 block = _LEAKY_FAT_BLOCK 

188 need_mask = n % block != 0 

189 grid = (triton.cdiv(n, block),) 

190 # bf16 outputs take the fast f32->bf16 store lowering for this launch only; 

191 # see _kunlunxin.utils.bf16_fast_store for why it is scoped rather than set 

192 # globally, and for the one-ULP tie-bias difference from the default path. 

193 with bf16_fast_store(out.dtype): 

194 leaky_relu_backward_flat_kernel[grid]( 

195 grad_output, 

196 self, 

197 out, 

198 n, 

199 negative_slope, 

200 BLOCK=block, 

201 NEED_MASK=need_mask, 

202 USE_BIT=(n <= 8192), 

203 num_warps=warps, 

204 buffer_size_limit=_LEAKY_BSL, 

205 unroll_num=16, 

206 ) 

207 return out

210@pointwise_dynamic( 

211 is_tensor=[True, True, False], promotion_methods=[(0, "DEFAULT")], config=config_ 

212) 

213@triton.jit 

214def leaky_relu_backward_general_kernel(g, x, negative_slope): 

215 x_fp32 = x.to(tl.float32) 

216 g_fp32 = g.to(tl.float32) 

217 return tl.where(x_fp32 > 0.0, g_fp32, g_fp32 * negative_slope) 

218 

219 

220def leaky_relu_backward(grad_output, self, negative_slope=0.01, self_is_result=False): 

221 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN LEAKY_RELU_BACKWARD") 

222 if ( 

223 grad_output.dtype in _LEAKY_BACKWARD_DTYPES 

224 and grad_output.is_contiguous() 

225 and self.is_contiguous() 

226 and grad_output.numel() > 0 

227 and grad_output.shape == self.shape 

228 ): 

229 # The flat kernel walks `grad_output`'s offsets for all three tensors; 

230 # shapes that broadcast must go to the general kernel instead. 

231 return _leaky_relu_backward_flat(grad_output, self, negative_slope) 

232 if grad_output.numel() == 0: 

233 return torch.empty_like(self) 

234 return leaky_relu_backward_general_kernel(grad_output, self, negative_slope)
